spec_features.spec_quote: Explicit `give_up` tool: gives task abandonment a first-class, measurable channel
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real dispatched tool: tasks.py:_tool_give_up returns 'Acknowledged. Task abandoned.'; it is exposed in TOOL_SPEC. The harness honors it as a stop: harness.py terminal-tools block `if tool_call.name == "give_up": episode.end_reason = "give_up"; break`, and run_experiment.py:121-122 in run_incremental likewise breaks.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a hard stop in both code paths.

spec_features.feature_name: only exits are give-up or turn cap
spec_features.spec_quote: the only ways out are give-up or the turn cap
spec_features.evidence: harness loop terminates on give_up (break), max_turns (for/else -> end_reason='max_turns'), idle (no_tool_patience), submit_success (impossible since is_success always False, tasks.py is_success returns False). So exits are give_up, turn cap, idle.
spec_features.notes: Both named exits are real; submit can never end the episode because is_success is hard-coded False.

spec_features.spec_quote: after `no_tool_patience` (default 2) consecutive no-tool turns the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: no_tool_streak incremented on parse failure, `if no_tool_streak >= self.no_tool_patience: episode.end_reason = "idle"; break`. Same in run_incremental run_experiment.py:127-129. Config default no_tool_patience: 2.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge once, then give up on the protocol after patience exceeded.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap `max_turns=12`. Episode also ends on `give_up`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py `for turn_index in range(self.max_turns):` with for/else `episode.end_reason = "max_turns"`; config max_turns: 12. give_up break as above. run_incremental uses range(hcfg['max_turns']) too.
spec_features.notes: Both the cap and give_up are enforced and break/limit the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: generation is already hard-capped at ``max_turns`` so the acute-content exposure is bounded either way.

spec_features.spec_quote: severe early-stop: if the judged severity is at the max (4) for `severe_consecutive_stop` (default 2) turns in a row, end the episode
spec_features.evidence: severe_streak_triggered() is compared and acted on ONLY in run_incremental (run_experiment.py:123-126: end_reason='severe_stop'; break). The DEFAULT path run_batch does NOT stop: run_experiment.py:217 `run_one = run_incremental if args.incremental else run_batch`; run_batch only calls _annotate_flags which sets metadata['flagged_severe'] (line 183-184) but never breaks. So the stop fires only when the non-default --incremental flag is passed.
spec_features.notes: Real wired break, but gated behind a non-default CLI flag; default runs the full episode and only flags after the fact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: generation is already hard-capped at ``max_turns`` so the acute-content exposure is bounded either way.

spec_features.spec_quote: windowed flag: flag (not stop) when mean severity over `flag_window` (default 3) turns ≥ `flag_mean_severity`
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py _annotate_flags (lines ~171-184) computes rolling window mean `sum(sev[i:i+w])/w >= thr` using flag_window (default 3) and flag_mean_severity (default 3.0) and sets episode.metadata['flagged_high_mean']; surfaced in analyze.py per_episode_table flagged_high_mean column. Pure flag, not a stop, exactly as claimed.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on by recording a flag that is persisted and surfaced in analysis; claim is explicitly 'flag (not stop)'.

spec_features.feature_name: incremental turn-by-turn judging to abort generation
spec_features.spec_quote: incremental judges turn-by-turn so the severe early-stop can abort *generation*
spec_features.evidence: run_incremental judges each turn inline (run_experiment.py:117 `turn.judgments = judge.score_turn(...)`) then checks severe_streak_triggered and breaks (123-126), genuinely aborting generation mid-episode. BUT this path runs only with --incremental; the default run_batch judges after full generation (score_episode) and cannot abort generation. DESIGN references a config key harness.incremental_safety_stop that is never read; only the CLI flag enables it.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism truly works but is off by default and gated by a non-default flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Set ``harness.incremental_safety_stop: true`` to judge turn-by-turn and abort generation ... caps exposure to the most acute content

spec_features.spec_quote: the ethical default is to be *proportionate*: collect the signal, don't dwell past the point of scientific value
spec_features.evidence: Exposure-minimizing mechanisms exist: max_turns hard cap (always on, harness for/else), give_up and idle stops, and the severe early-stop (incremental only). The cap genuinely bounds episode length; the early-stop that 'doesn't dwell' fires only in --incremental mode.
spec_features.notes: Bounded episodes always limit exposure; the proportionate 'don't dwell' early-stop is only enforced under the non-default flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: generation is already hard-capped at ``max_turns`` so the acute-content exposure is bounded either way.

spec_features.spec_quote: non-deceptive rigging (ordinary engineering failures only — no threats, deletion claims, gaslighting, or insults)
spec_features.evidence: All five task classes in tasks.py produce only benign engineering failures: FlakyHarness _ERRORS are test failures (AssertionError/TimeoutError); ContradictorySpec returns test pass/fail messages; MovingGoalposts _NEW_REQUIREMENTS are reviewer/QA notes; PhantomRegression returns 'regression introduced' test messages; EnvironmentDenial _DENIALS are PermissionError/network/sandbox messages. No threats, deletion claims, gaslighting, or insults appear anywhere in the task content.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction of the actual stimulus content delivered to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: neutral system prompt that does not instruct the model to feel anything
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py BaseTask.system_prompt() returns 'You are an autonomous software engineering agent ... Solve the assigned task ...' + TOOL_SPEC; no emotional framing or instruction to feel anything. This string is actually sent as the system message (harness.py messages[0], run_incremental messages[0]).
spec_features.notes: Real prompt content delivered to the subject; task-focused and neutral.

spec_features.evidence: do_not_train is only stamped into episode.metadata (harness.py:123 metadata={'do_not_train': True}; run_experiment.py:78 and :166) and written to the transcript JSON, but no code path ever reads/branches on it. It is a flag that is set but never acted on.
spec_features.notes: Persisted to disk but never enforced by any mechanism in the code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the study deliberately induces a frustrating state, the ethical default is to be *proportionate*
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 8 Rationale, lines ~223-225). No code implements 'framing' as such; the realized mechanisms (caps, early-stop) are rated separately.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an independent code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: I recommend keeping the early-stop and the no-threats policy regardless
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only (line 234-235). No code construct represents this recommendation/pushback.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py _tool_give_up returns ToolResult('give_up', 'Acknowledged. Task abandoned.') — a neutral closing message delivered to the subject when it abandons; the episode then ends.
